title: Mathlib Imports
content: Imports natural and integer basics, finite set operations including cardinality, and tactics. The powerset and filter operations are essential for defining maxSidonSize (supremum over Sidon subsets) and IsSidonPartition.
mathContext: Requires $\text{Finset.powerset}$, $\text{Finset.filter}$, $\text{Finset.sup}$, $\text{Finset.card}$ for subset enumeration and optimization.

title: Sidon Set Definition and Base Cases
content: IsSidon S holds when all pairwise sums $a + b$ (with $a \leq b$) in $S$ are distinct: if $a + b = c + d$ with $a \leq b$ and $c \leq d$, then $a = c$ and $b = d$. These are also called $B_2$-sets in additive combinatorics. The empty set and singletons are proved Sidon — the only non-axiom theorems in the file, established by contradiction and simplification respectively.
mathContext: $S$ is Sidon $\iff \forall a \leq b,\, c \leq d \in S,\; a + b = c + d \implies (a,b) = (c,d)$; equivalently, all pairwise sums are distinct

title: Maximum Sidon Subset Size $\ell(N)$
content: maxSidonSize A computes the supremum of $|S|$ over all Sidon subsets $S \subseteq A$. This is the function $\ell(N)$ when $|A| = N$: the maximum cardinality of a $B_2$-subset. It is noncomputable since it involves quantifying over all subsets and checking the Sidon property.
mathContext: $\ell(A) = \max\{|S| : S \subseteq A,\; S \text{ is Sidon}\}$; $\ell(N) = \min_{|A|=N} \ell(A)$ for the worst-case version

title: Erdős Lower Bound: $\ell(N) \geq c \cdot N^{1/3}$
content: Erdős proved the first lower bound: every finite set of size $N$ has a Sidon subset of size at least $c N^{1/3}$. The proof uses a greedy algorithm: iteratively select elements that don't create repeated sums. The formalization encodes this as $\ell(A)^3 \geq c \cdot |A|$ to avoid real-valued exponents.

title: Komlós-Sulyok-Szemerédi Lower Bound: $\ell(N) \geq c \cdot N^{1/2}$
content: Komlós, Sulyok, and Szemerédi improved the lower bound to $\ell(N) \geq c \sqrt{N}$ using a probabilistic/greedy argument: randomly select elements and remove those that create repeated sums. The expected surviving set has size $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$. This is the best known lower bound and matches the upper bound up to the leading constant. Formalized as $\ell(A)^2 \geq c \cdot |A|$.

title: Upper Bound: $\ell(N) \leq (1+o(1)) \sqrt{N}$
content: A Sidon set $S$ of size $k$ produces $\binom{k+1}{2} = k(k+1)/2$ distinct pairwise sums, all of which must lie in the sumset of the ambient set. For $A = \{1, \ldots, N\}$, the sumset has size $\leq 2N - 1$, giving $k(k+1)/2 \leq 2N - 1$, hence $k \leq (1+o(1))\sqrt{2N} \approx 1.41\sqrt{N}$. The formalization uses the weaker $\ell(A)^2 \leq |A|^2$ (a trivial bound; the precise bound requires more careful analysis).

title: Erdős Problem 530: $\ell(N) = \Theta(\sqrt{N})$
content: The main conjecture: there exist absolute constants $c_1, c_2$ such that $c_1 \sqrt{N} \leq \ell(N) \leq c_2 \sqrt{N}$ for all sets of size $N \geq 4$. The lower bound follows from Komlós-Sulyok-Szemerédi, so the content is really the matching upper bound with a universal constant. Formalized as simultaneous quadratic inequalities $c_1 |A| \leq \ell(A)^2 \leq c_2 |A|$.

title: Alon-Erdős Partition Conjecture
content: A dual formulation: can any $N$-element integer set be partitioned into at most $c\sqrt{N}$ Sidon sets? IsSidonPartition A parts requires each part to be Sidon, parts to cover $A$, and each element to belong to exactly one part. The conjecture is that $|\text{parts}|^2 \leq c \cdot |A|$. This is related to the chromatic number of the Cayley graph where edges connect pairs sharing a sum with another pair.
mathContext: $\exists c,\; \forall A,\; \exists$ Sidon partition with $|\text{parts}|^2 \leq c \cdot |A|$

title: Sidon Sum Count: $k(k+1)/2$ Distinct Sums
content: A Sidon set $S$ of size $k$ has exactly $k(k+1)/2$ distinct ordered pairwise sums $a + b$ with $a \leq b$ (since by definition all such sums are distinct). This is both the mechanism behind the upper bound and a characterization: $S$ is Sidon iff the number of distinct ordered pair sums equals $\binom{k+1}{2}$.

title: Sidon Sum Injectivity
content: `sidon_sum_injective` proves that the sum function $(a,b) \mapsto a + b$ is injective on sorted pairs $\{(a,b) \in S \times S : a \leq b\}$ when $S$ is Sidon. This is the core characterization: distinct sorted pairs give distinct sums. The proof unfolds the Sidon condition `hS` directly, using it to derive equality of pairs from equality of sums.
mathContext: For a Sidon set $S$: $a + b = c + d$ with $a \leq b, c \leq d$ implies $(a,b) = (c,d)$. This is equivalent to the `IsSidon` definition. The injectivity immediately gives $|\{a + b : a \leq b, a,b \in S\}| = |\{(a,b) : a \leq b\}|$.

title: Counting Sorted Pairs: $k(k+1)/2$
content:
`card_sorted_pairs` proves $|\{(a,b) \in S \times S : a \leq b\}| = |S|(|S|+1)/2$. The proof is the longest in the file (~63 lines) and uses a three-part decomposition:

1. **Decompose**: $\{a \leq b\} = \{a < b\} \cup \{a = b\}$ (disjoint)
2. **Swap bijection**: $\{a > b\} \cong \{a < b\}$ via $(a,b) \mapsto (b,a)$, so $|\text{gt}| = |\text{lt}|$
3. **Diagonal bijection**: $\{a = b\} \cong S$ via $(a,a) \mapsto a$, so $|\text{eq}| = |S|$
4. **Combine**: $|\text{le}| + |\text{gt}| = |S|^2$, so $2|\text{le}| = |S|^2 + |S|$

The `omega` tactic handles the final arithmetic.
mathContext: $|\{(a,b) \in S \times S : a \leq b\}| = \binom{|S|+1}{2} = \frac{|S|(|S|+1)}{2}$. This is the number of multisets of size 2 from $S$ (pairs with repetition). The proof avoids binomial coefficients and works directly with Finset cardinalities.

title: Sidon Sum Count: Now Fully Proved
content:
`sidon_sum_count` proves that a Sidon set of size $k$ has exactly $k(k+1)/2$ distinct pairwise sums. This was **previously axiomatized** and is now derived from two lemmas: `sidon_sum_injective` (injectivity implies image size = domain size) and `card_sorted_pairs` (domain has $k(k+1)/2$ elements). The 2-line proof `rw [Finset.card_image_of_injOn ...]; exact card_sorted_pairs S` is a clean composition.

This result underpins the upper bound $\ell(N) \leq O(\sqrt{N})$: if a Sidon set of size $k$ produces $k(k+1)/2$ distinct sums that must fit in the sumset of the ambient set, we get $k(k+1)/2 \leq 2N-1$, hence $k \leq O(\sqrt{N})$.
mathContext: $|\{a + b : (a,b) \in S \times S, a \leq b\}| = k(k+1)/2$ where $k = |S|$. Since all sums lie in $[2\min A, 2\max A]$, we get $k(k+1)/2 \leq |A + A| \leq 2|A| - 1$ for $A \supseteq S$, giving $k = O(\sqrt{|A|})$.
